thread.title: Don't Buy Apple Stock on Thursday's Pop - TheStreet

author: Home
title: Don't Buy Apple Stock on Thursday's Pop - TheStreet
text:
Apple ( AAPL ) is up some 2% to $225 as I write this Thursday, rising after JPMorgan Chase initiated the stock with an "Overweight" rating and a $272 price target. But my plan is to buy this stock intelligently, and the charts say I should skip Thursday's run-up and only buy Apple closer to $220.
Now, I'm already short a series of cascading AAPL put options that expire in November, but I really need to re-establish a core long position in the stock so that I can write call options against it. That strategy will add more revenue to my portfolio without increasing capital risk.
Yes, there are always plenty of reasons to worry about Apple in the short term. For instance, Qualcomm ( QCOM ) recently claimed that Apple was stealing trade secrets and passing them on to Intel ( INTC ) in an effort to do an end-run around Qualcomm's place as an Apple supplier. AAPL also recently had to juggle its order flow between Pegatron and Foxconn ( HNHAF ) after production on Apple's new iPhone XR production fell behind schedule.
Such headlines bog down Apple at times, but the company's shareholders always seem to triumph in the end. Why? Because Apple is in the midst of transforming itself from a company that makes and sells smartphones and other hardware into one that benefits from subscriptions and services.

Consider the recent news that Gene Munster of Loup Ventures estimated that AAPL is converting Apple Music listeners into paying customers at 2.5 times the rate that Spotify ( SPOT ) does. Whoa baby!
Spotify still controls 62% share of the global music-streaming business, but that's off of a 65% high. By contrast, Apple's share is growing and now stands at 34%, and the company still has plenty of room to expand this market share by tapping into its existing "ecosystem" of products. In fact, Apple's music service has so far only managed to subscribe roughly 6.3% of its 780 million active users. That means there's still 93.7% to go, gang.
That alone is a reason to own Apple rather than trade it, as Jim Cramer often says. Oh, I've made some dough trading in and out of the stock, but I would have done a lot better if I had just made the name a core position in my portfolio instead.
So why am I waiting to buy the stock at around $220? Well first, I don't really want to buy Apple (or any other stock) on a "up" day -- that's an amateur move. But more importantly, Apple's chart shows that the stock has adhered to a "pitchfork" pattern all year long:
I'd love to buy AAPL at close to the lower trend line of this pitchfork pattern (the area circled in red above). Getting the stock at $210 is probably unrealistic right now, but what about $220 by mid-October?
All we'd need is a broad-market sell-off for that to happen. We wouldn't even need some stock-specific bad news.
So, my plan is to buy Apple at $220 or better within two weeks -- or if I must, $225 or better within four weeks. For a target price to sell it at, let's shoot for $265.
